label: Required by a being's end: x is a means without which y's own end cannot be attained (a primitive)
term: required by a being's end (the EndRequires parameter)
definition: EndRequires y x, for beings y and x: x is required by y's own end in the teleological means-to-end sense, that is, x is a means without which the good that y's appetite (natural or rational) is ordered to cannot be attained, as food for one who wills to live or a ship for one who wills to cross the sea. It is not strict modal co-existence: that x exists wherever y exists, or that x exists necessarily, does not make EndRequires y x true. A primitive Lean parameter of type B → B → Prop of TruthCore.Causality.NarDerivation, constrained only by the open premises that use it: WN (RationalFixedGivingIsRequired, a rational power is fixed toward a given being only if that being is required by the giver's end) and SS (ActualRootsEndRequiresNoOther, no being other than an actual root is required by its end). No structural property (reflexivity, transitivity) is assumed; it is world-free, like the will bridges of #1941.
note: Analyst primitive, attribution deferred (docs/notes/nar-derivation.md). Intended reading (navigation only, not attributed; paraphrased, not quoted): ST I q.19 a.3 co. and q.82 a.1, where the will adheres of necessity to its last end and to what the end cannot be had without, as one who wills to live wills food, but not to other means. Examples: an animal's flourishing requires food; a voyage requires a ship. Non-examples: a generous person's goodness does not require the particular gifts given; on classical theism, the divine goodness requires no creature, being complete without other things (q.19 a.3, paraphrase). Distinct from causal or grounding dependence: x can be required by y's end without either grounding the other. REJECTED READING: the strict-modal reading (x exists at every accessible world where y exists; TruthCore.Causality.NarDerivation.StrictModalRequirement). On it every NECESSARY_2 being is required by every end, WN is trivial for necessary effects, and SS with a common root alone yields NAR (NarDerivation Model.Laws 6), so the will route N3 would beg the question and the emanationist rival would deny SS rather than WN. OPEN semantic obligations: (1) that the means-to-end reading is not covertly modal, i.e. a criterion of 'cannot be attained without' that does not reduce to co-existence across worlds; (2) whether 'end' applies univocally to a first source; (3) whether the necessary diffusion of the good counts as the end requiring its effects or as a fixity without requirement (the latter is how WN's rival is stated, note section 5).
